task: Align AssistantFactory.build's projectModelOverride whitelist check with enforce_allowed_model so an unconfigured project whitelist no longer drops skill-enabled builtin subagents and sub-assistants when a request names llm_model, make the swallowed failure log informative, and add unit tests.

key_reasoning.reason: Three service-layer components are touched: the AssistantFactory.build whitelist check, the failure logging in LangGraphAssistantBuilder.create_subagent_executors, and the failure logging in create_assistant_executors. All of them reuse the existing core policy helper enforce_allowed_model or resolve_requested_model. AssistantFactory has only two instantiation sites, both in the subagent path.

The root cause is confirmed and the fix direction is stated. Several design choices are still open: whether a configured empty [] whitelist means deny-all (as in enforce_allowed_model) or unrestricted (as in resolve_requested_model), whether to honour the is_global exemption, whether to fall back or raise for a sub-assistant in a different project, and whether to remove the redundant pre-check entirely. Each of these is a light question with an existing precedent, not an open architectural decision.

The closest pattern is enforce_allowed_model in core/dependecies.py. It already covers the security-sensitive None vs [] distinction, and tests pin it (test_dependecies.py), so no divergence bump applies. Base score is S. One bump applies because the model whitelist is a project-level access-control policy and the change relaxes a hard block. Fixing ExtendedHTTPException.__str__ globally would be broader, but it is avoidable by formatting the log locally.

About 2-3 source files are modified (assistant_factory.py, assistant_engine_builder.py, possibly model_availability_service.py). Tests go into the existing test_assistant_factory.py, plus possibly one new builder test file. The work spans the src service tree and the tests tree. This calibrates to the S example epmcdme-10102 (3 files, adjacent directories).

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S to M: the change affects authorization-like policy (project model whitelist enforcement under projectModelOverride)
